source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 13:1–18 binds Hebrew 13:2–19; chapters 14–18 align directly. Hebrew 13:1 is excluded because the preceding batch binds it to public 12:32. All 134 original XML records, including their written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

key_decisions.decision: Supplies debts from the following rule while retaining release as the key term; apparatus acknowledges disagreement about permanent remission versus suspension.
Retains creditor action, the neighbor/brother relationship, and the proclamation without silently deciding the disputed duration of release.
Preserves the law's unequal treatment of foreigner and fellow Israelite instead of universalizing the permission.
Keeps the no-poor assurance tied grammatically to the next verse's condition, without harmonizing away verse 11.
Makes the release-year calculation audible as inner speech; retains grudging sight, withholding, the poor person's appeal, and liability for sin.
Preserves the explicit ongoing poverty statement alongside verse 4's conditional assurance, and repeats the open-hand image.
Names sale, both sexes, six years of service and seventh-year freedom; does not present slavery as ordinary employment.
Returns to the source's male example and preserves the stated motives without implying every slave's situation was chosen.
Keeps bodily piercing, the door, permanent slavery, and the female-slave clause; the note flags the disputed scope of do the same.
Retains the difficult double-wage comparison rather than changing six years to a presumed hired-worker contract length.
